title: Bengaluru - Painting & Repainting Deduction Beyond Normal Wear and Tear
layer_1_raw_input: I lived in Koramangala Bengaluru for 3 years. Moved out on 1st November 2025. Security deposit was Rs 1,00,000. Landlord returned 70,000 and deducted 30,000 for full house repainting. We had a written lease agreement which did not mention mandatory painting deduction upon exit. The walls only had normal wear and tear and no physical damage.

FORMAL NOTICE FOR REFUND OF SECURITY DEPOSIT

Date: 08 November 2026

To,
V. Suresh Reddy
(Landlord / Property Owner)
Property: Flat 204, Green Glen Apartments, 4th Block Koramangala, Bengaluru 560034

From,
Karthik Subramanian
(Former Tenant)
Contact: [Tenant Phone / Email]

Subject: Formal Demand for Immediate Refund of Outstanding Security Deposit of ₹30,000

Dear V. Suresh Reddy,

I am issuing this formal demand notice regarding the residential premises situated at:
Flat 204, Green Glen Apartments, 4th Block Koramangala, Bengaluru 560034.

1. TENANCY PARTICULARS:
I was residing as a tenant at the above-mentioned premises and peacefully handed over vacant possession upon moving out on 1 November 2025. The tenancy was governed by a written rental agreement executed between us.

2. SECURITY DEPOSIT ACCOUNTING:
The agreed security deposit of ₹100,000 was tendered to you upon commencing the tenancy.
To date, you have returned ₹70,000, leaving an unpaid deposit balance of ₹30,000.

3. UNJUSTIFIED WITHHOLDING / DEDUCTIONS:
You have purportedly withheld/deducted ₹30,000 citing 'full house repainting'. Please take note that under applicable law, specifically Section 15 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Division of maintenance responsibilities and routine wear and tear); Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee (Reasonable wear and tear excepted)), a security deposit is held in trust solely to secure against tenant breach or damage beyond reasonable wear and tear. Arbitrary deductions without providing itemized repair bills, GST invoices, and prior joint inspection records are legally impermissible and constitute unjust retention of funds.

4. LEGAL POSITION:
Under applicable Indian statutes, specifically Section 15 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Division of maintenance responsibilities and routine wear and tear); Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee (Reasonable wear and tear excepted)), a landlord is legally required to return the security deposit promptly upon vacant handover, subject only to demonstrable, itemized actual loss beyond reasonable wear and tear. Unilateral deductions without documentary proof and verified invoices amount to breach of trust and unlawful retention of tenant funds.

5. FORMAL DEMAND:
You are hereby called upon to refund the outstanding sum of ₹30,000 within 15 (fifteen) days from the receipt of this notice, payable to the following bank account / UPI ID:
Payment Details: [Your Bank Name, Account Number, IFSC Code or UPI ID]

In the event of failure to refund the said sum within 15 days, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal remedies before the competent Rent Authority, Civil Court, Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, or approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / Lok Adalat for recovery, holding you liable for all legal expenses, damages, and statutory interest.

Sincerely,

Karthik Subramanian
(Former Tenant)

# PRE-LITIGATION CASE DOSSIER & COMPLAINT PETITION

**BEFORE THE HON'BLE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION /**  
**BEFORE THE SECRETARY, DISTRICT LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITY (DLSA)**  
**AT BENGALURU, KARNATAKA**

---

### IN THE MATTER OF:
**TENANT / COMPLAINANT**  
*(Details as per Lease Agreement)*  
`... COMPLAINANT`

**VERSUS**

**LANDLORD / OPPOSITE PARTY**  
*(Property Owner / Lessor)*  
`... OPPOSITE PARTY`

---

## 1. SYNOPSIS & LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS

| Date | Event / Fact | Statutory Nexus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tenancy Inception** | Complainant entered into residential tenancy in Bengaluru, Karnataka and transferred ₹100,000 as refundable security deposit. | Section 10, Indian Contract Act, 1872 & Section 61, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 |
| **1 November 2025** | Complainant lawfully vacated premises and peacefully surrendered keys following joint handover. | Section 108(q), Transfer of Property Act, 1882 |
| **+30 Days Post-Exit** | Statutory 30-day refund window elapsed. Opposite Party failed to return full deposit or tender itemized GST invoices. | Section 11, Model Tenancy Act, 2021 |
| **Dispute Date** | Opposite Party unilaterally withheld ₹30,000 under the pretext of 'full house repainting', without supplying third-party contractor tax invoices. | Section 73 & 74, Indian Contract Act, 1872 |
| **Notice Served** | Complainant served formal 15-day statutory demand notice requesting refund or production of genuine GST bills. | Consumer Protection Act, 2019 §2(11) |
| **Present Date** | Opposite Party failed to comply. Present complaint/conciliation petition instituted for recovery of ₹31,200. | Section 21, Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 |

---

## 2. STATUTORY GROUNDS & STATEMENT OF CLAIM

1. **Unilateral Breach of Contract (Section 73, Indian Contract Act, 1872):**  
   The security deposit was delivered in trust solely to guarantee tenancy covenants. A landlord cannot unilaterally deduct funds for 'full house repainting' without proving actual, non-remote financial injury through certified receipts.

2. **Violation of Statutory Notice and Billing Mandate (Section 11, Model Tenancy Act, 2021):**  
   Section 11 strictly mandates that any deduction must be substantiated with itemized accounts and actual expenditure bills. In the absence of third-party contractor GST invoices, withholding constitutes an arbitrary penalty barred under Section 74 of the ICA.

3. **Admissibility of Electronic Records (Section 61, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023):**  
   The Complainant substantiates all financial transactions (deposit transfer of ₹100,000 and partial return of ₹70,000) through bank account statements and UPI transaction logs, forming admissible primary electronic evidence.

4. **Deficiency of Service (Section 2(11), Consumer Protection Act, 2019):**  
   The arbitrary retention of tenancy deposits by a landlord constitutes an unfair practice and deficiency in service, entitling the consumer to restitution and compensation.

---

## 3. PRAYER & RELIEF SOUGHT

WHEREFORE, the Complainant respectfully prays that this Hon'ble Authority / Commission may be pleased to:

* **A. Direct the Opposite Party** to immediately refund the unlawfully withheld principal sum of **₹30,000** to the Complainant.
* **B. Award Statutory Interest** of **₹1,200** (calculated @ 8% p.a. from expiry of 30 days post move-out till actual realization) under the Interest Act, 1978.
* **C. Grant Reasonable Litigation Costs & Nominal Compensation** of ₹5,000/- for mental harassment and unjust deprivation of hard-earned funds.
* **D. Pass any other order(s)** deemed just and equitable in the interest of justice.

---

## 4. INDEX OF ANNEXURES (FILING CHECKLIST)

| Annexure No. | Document Description | Evidentiary Purpose |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **Annexure C-1** | Copy of Signed Lease / Tenancy Agreement (or statement of oral tenancy terms). | Proves contractual relationship and agreed refund covenants. |
| **Annexure C-2** | Certified Bank Statement / UPI Transaction Log of deposit debit. | Primary electronic evidence under BSA 2023 §61 proving deposit remittance. |
| **Annexure C-3** | Move-Out Inspection Record / WhatsApp Key Handover Confirmation. | Confirms peaceful surrender without contemporaneous objection. |
| **Annexure C-4** | Copy of 15-Day Statutory Legal Demand Notice served on Landlord. | Proves pre-litigation notice requirement was satisfied. |
| **Annexure C-5** | Proof of Service (India Post Registered AD Tracking / WhatsApp Delivery). | Establishes delivery and opposite party's default. |

---

### 5. VERIFICATION
I, the Complainant above-named, do hereby verify and state that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 4 above are true and correct to my personal knowledge and belief derived from contractual records, and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at **Bengaluru** on this **08 November 2026**.

*(Complainant / Deponent)*
